_about: THE STONE WALL BESIDE A LEVEL NARROWER THAN THE WINDOW (planning step 284; sim/SideWalls.hpp). ENHANCED, not the original: the view is 256 units tall and 256 x the window's
shape wide, and the camera centres a level narrower than that, so a window wider than 16:9 showed only the sky, or black, beyond the level's two sides (a player's report).
On a level whose two sides its own static collision closes over the whole height, each strip is drawn as a stone wall: the game's own double_block_plat, stood on end, in
the brightness variant of the level's own blocks, at most three columns of it, fading into plain black. A picture only: no collision, nothing the simulation reads. A level
with an open side keeps the frame it had. `enabled: false` draws the frame as it was before step 284.
PROVENANCE. THE OWNER'S RULING, 2026-11-28, on the mock-ups (option F, with the super-wide pictures 'at most three rows, then dark'): 'this is it! This is the best one!',
then 'go'. THE NUMBERS ARE THE MOCK'S (its script, kept outside git): columns of the block 31 units apart (so two overlap by 1), pieces 128 long every 125 down the height,
every second column's first row at 0 and the others' at 62, a quarter turn, at most 3 columns, black from the fade's end outward, a smoothstep fade from 76 to 94 units
beyond the edge (the third column ends at 94). Chosen for the build and not shown to the owner as numbers, `_guess: true`: closed_reach_units, backing_reach_units,
margin_units, fade_steps, fade_cap_units, world_default_variants, light_height_units, z_first, z_step.

_closed_reach_units: A side is closed when the vertical line this far outside the level's edge is covered, from y 0 to the level's height, by the rectangles of the walls below. Measured over
the 128 converted levels: 2-23 and 2-24 (level22a, level23a: 460 wide) stand their right wall at x 462, 2 units outside the edge, so under 2 units 102 levels are closed
and from 2 units 104; 8 units gives 104 as well. 4 leaves room beside the 2 and stays far short of a wall that stands well out: 1-08 and 1-27 are 704 wide with their
right wall at x 768, 64 units out, and are open.
_solid_entities: The original's invisible walls: static, unmoving, unbreakable, each one upright rectangle. Nothing else counts, so that a piece that breaks, moves or is taken away can
never close a side. Over the 128 levels the same 104 are closed if every static piece without a role is counted as well, so no level depends on the choice.
_entities: Read from the original's entities/ when the level's art is built, as black_bar.ent is (art.json black_bar): the stone's picture, its <EmissiveColor>, its applyLight and
static and its <Normal> are the .ent's own. The black is black_bar.ent's picture, black in every texel. No picture of this port's own is committed or made.
_variants: The stone takes the suffix most of the level's own placements of the block families carry (a tie goes to the world's default). The world's default, for a level that
places none, is what that world's levels mostly place (worlds 0 to 3, chapters 1 to 4): counted over the converted levels, chapter 1 places the plain blocks, chapter 2
the no-emissive, chapter 3 the low-emissive, and chapter 4 both the plain and the no-emissive, the plain on more levels. Only 4-02 and 4-18 place none, and both are open.
side_walls._light_height_units: The depth the stone's lights are measured at: a level's own blocks stand at z 0.
side_walls._backing_reach_units: Black from the edge outward. A 48:9 window is 1365 units wide, so beside the narrowest level (456) it shows 455 a side; 2048 covers any window up to 17:1.
side_walls._margin_units: The backing and the fade run this far above and below the level, so an earthquake's band beside a side shows black and not sky. The black bars reach x 0 to 768 only.
_fade_steps: Flat black slices side by side between the two, each at the smoothstep's value at its middle: the largest step of alpha between two slices is 1.5 / 64 = 0.023, and a
slice is 0.28 units, 0.8 px at 720 lines and 2.4 px at 2160.
side_walls._fade_cap_units: A last slice of whole black beyond the fade's end, over the outer stones' edge.
_depths: In the layer's z: in front of everything the scene draws (the markers' boxes stand at 0.5) and behind the black bars (1.0, art.json black_bar). The backings first, then
the stones, then the fade's slices, each piece z_step in front of the one before it, so no two are tied. Nothing the level draws is beyond a closed side on a 16:9
screen, where the camera never leaves the level.
